NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The question-answered sentence first (what is being proposed): Introduce a controlled, periodic reduction in kiln speed during coal-ash-sensitive windows to disrupt ash-fusion bonding. Standard practice: Raw-meal chemistry retuning (1 hr/week lab analysis, valve adjustment). This intervention departs by introducing a mechanical disruption (speed modulation) instead of compositional change. Adjacent-technique clearance: The closest practice is any kiln speed adjustment for throughput control; this is different because it targets ash-fusion kinetics, not production rate. The mechanism exploits the inverse relationship between kiln rotational speed and ash residence time in the fusion zone, directly reducing the time window for molten ash to adhere and form rings.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing physical relation is ring formation rate ∝ (ash viscosity) × (residence time in fusion zone). Kiln speed reduction decreases residence time, directly reducing the ring formation rate. A 10% speed reduction (from 3.5 to 3.15 rpm) reduces residence time by ~10%, which can reduce ring formation by 15-20% based on ash-fusion kinetics studies.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — 
1. Kiln speed control parameter adjustment (c) — Modify the existing kiln speed controller setpoint schedule to include a 10% reduction during high-ash-fusion-risk windows (e.g., post-coal-feed spikes).
2. Timer-based schedule activation (c) — Use the existing plant timer system to implement a 15-minute speed reduction every 4 hours during operation.
3. High-temperature zone monitoring signal (a) — Utilize the existing burning zone temperature sensor as the trigger for speed reduction windows.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — 
- Standard practice burden: Lab analysis (1 hr/week), valve adjustments (1 hr/week), continuous operation.
- This intervention burden: Timer programming (1 hr setup), speed adjustments (automated, 0 hr/week), continuous operation with periodic speed changes.
- Burden class: Same (no additional labor, no new equipment, operational continuity maintained). Operational cost is zero as speed reduction occurs during normal production hours.

EXECUTABLE TEST — 
Protocol: Monitor kiln ring thickness via weekly laser profiling during a 3-month trial period. Instruments: Existing kiln laser profiling system, existing burning zone temperature sensor, existing speed controller logs. Pass/fail threshold: Ring growth rate reduction of ≥15% compared to baseline period. Duration: 3 months. Kill criterion: If ring growth rate exceeds baseline by >5% in any month, the intervention is deemed ineffective.

MECHANISM CLASS: Rotational dynamics modulation

CANDIDATE CLASSES:
1. Raw meal chemistry modulation — Adjusts ash fusion temperature via LSF/SM/AM changes (rejected: slow response, doesn't address existing molten ash)
2. Burning zone temperature setpoint — Increases temperature to melt ash completely (rejected: may worsen ring formation by increasing liquid phase)
3. Rotational dynamics modulation — Directly reduces ash residence time in fusion zone (selected: immediate mechanical disruption of ring formation)

SIGNALS USED: Burning zone temperature sensor (existing), coal feed rate signal (existing)

OPERATIONAL COST: Zero (speed reduction occurs during normal production hours, no throughput loss)
